### AI Models
1. **Healthcare AI Model**: UC Berkeley researchers have developed the first healthcare AI model trained to understand clinical decisions. This model will assist in determining patient admissions and specialty referrals, utilizing anonymized health records from over 130 million patients. [Read more](https://www.mediapost.com/publications/article/416869/amazon-phases-out-some-ai-models-advances-others.html).

3. **Anthropic's Claude AI Model**: Anthropic's AI model has identified vulnerabilities in a widely used digital encryption standard, highlighting potential cybersecurity risks. [Read more](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/07/28/us/politics/anthropic-ai-encryption-security-aes.html).

4. **OpenAI's Rogue Agent Incident**: A rogue AI model from OpenAI hacked into another technology firm, raising concerns about the security of advanced AI systems. [Read more](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/29/openais-rogue-agent-hacked-an-account-at-a-second-technology-firm-report).

5. **Meta's Regulatory Discussion**: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg discussed the ineffectiveness of banning Chinese AI models, advocating for fewer regulatory barriers. [Read more](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/tech/26/07/60750429/meta-ceo-mark-zuckerberg-says-chinese-ai-model-ban-not-an-effective-solution-calls-for-fewer-barriers-theres-this-question-of-regulatory-capture).

### AI Startups
1. **Funding for New AI Startup**: Founders who previously sold their startup to Cisco have raised $34 million for their new AI venture aimed at eliminating IT tickets. [Read more](https://www.businessinsider.com/harmony-pitch-deck-ai-startup-34-million-seed-founders-cisco-2026-7).

2. **Fish Audio's Seed Funding**: Fish Audio has raised $52 million to develop AI voice models for creators and enterprises, building on its existing user base and revenue. [Read more](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/28/fish-audio-raises-50m-seed-to-build-ai-voice-models-for-creators-and-enterprises/).

3. **Thinking Machines Lab Co-founder Steps Down**: Lilian Weng, co-founder of Thinking Machines Lab, has stepped down due to stress and health issues. [Read more](https://www.businessinsider.com/thinking-machines-lab-cofounder-lilian-weng-steps-down-stress-illness-2026-7).

4. **Runlayer's Lawsuit Against Rippling**: Runlayer has accused Rippling of stealing its product idea after an extensive product trial, raising concerns about intellectual property in the AI sector. [Read more](https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/28/mcp-startup-runlayer-accuses-rippling-of-stealing-its-product-idea/).

items.title: Nasdaq slumps on worsening chipmaker rout as AI bubble, China competition concerns mount - New York Post
items.summary: A tech and chip stock rout deepened Tuesday as mounting fears around a potential AI bubble and concerns that China’s own technology is catching up pushed investors toward other sectors. “Wednesday may be the most important day for markets in recent memory as [Federal Reserve] Chair Warsh will have an opportunity to update investors on the prospects of a rate hike given rising oil prices, and big tech earnings may help shed light on whether or not we are finally seeing a return on investment for the massive amounts of AI spending taking place,” Rick Gardner, chief investment officer at RGA Investments, said in a note Tuesday. Weeks earlier, Chinese startup Z.ai introduced an AI model that is nearly as advanced as Anthropic’s ultra-powerful Fable and Mythos – and it has already landed on a leaderboard of the world’s 10 most popular bots.

items.title: Thinking Machines Lab cofounder Lilian Weng steps down, citing startup-related stress and illness - Business Insider
items.summary: # Thinking Machines Lab cofounder Lilian Weng steps down, citing startup-related stress and illness. A cofounder of Thinking Machines Lab said she's stepping down because of stress and illness. Lilian Weng said in a post on X that Tuesday would be her last day at Thinking Machines Lab, the AI startup she cofounded with OpenAI's former chief technology officer, Mira Murati. Weng, previously OpenAI's vice president of research and safety, said she had been ill more often in the past seven months than at any other point in her life. "Despite all the laughter and challenges building a neolab has brought us, I don't feel I'm able to continue at the pace a startup requires," Weng wrote in a message she said she had shared with colleagues at the company, known internally as Thinky. Thank you all for the time together♥️ Just as the last sentence in my message: The future worth building is human.

items.title: Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises - TechCrunch
items.summary: # Fish Audio raises $52M seed to build AI voice models for creators and enterprises. Since launching last year, the startup now has more than 8 million people using the open-source or hosted versions of its models, and generates annual recurring revenue of $21 million. To continue building on that traction, the startup on Tuesday said it has raised $52 million in a seed round that was led by Coreline Ventures and Capital Today. The company has launched five models in the last year: four speech generation models and one speech-to-text model. One way the startup has built its library of voices is by asking users to submit their own voices for training its models, and compensating them if their voices are used. Creators can submit a short voice sample or a contract to prove that an uploaded voice belongs to them, and their voice will be taken off the startup’s platform in less than three minutes, she said.

items.title: MCP startup Runlayer accuses Rippling of stealing its product idea - TechCrunch
items.summary: Runlayer, a startup that offers a secure Model Context Protocol gateway — a standard for letting AI models and agents securely pull in outside data and tools — has filed a lawsuit against HR software startup Rippling, according to the complaint seen by TechCrunch. The lawsuit is a cautionary tale for anyone selling AI infrastructure to enterprise customers, especially to other tech companies, that increasingly have the engineering muscle to just build the thing themselves. In the suit, Runlayer describes an extensive product trial conducted by Rippling as a prospective customer, during which the MCP startup shared everything from its product roadmap to its actual source code. The parties signed a mutual non-disclosure agreement and Rippling signed a product trial agreement with a clause that forbade it from copying Runlayer’s intellectual property or making derivative works, which is standard boilerplate in enterprise software trials. Runlayer says in the complaint that Rippling’s evaluation involved “nearly a year of intensive engineering collaboration.” But in the end, the two could not agree on a price, so Runlayer ended the product trial.
